name: quintessence

attributes.attribute: from Latin for five and distilled essence
one of five provinces of Ireland
boundless shifting space before the medieval period

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Quintessence is a cosmological concept. The word springs from Latin for five and a distilled essence. It points to the mystical center, Mide. Mide is a place both everywhere and nowhere, a pivot the world turns around. Mide was one of five kingdom provinces of old Ireland. Until the medieval era it stayed bound to no single site. Earlier the center hung as an unbounded, drifting span. Both Uisneach and Tara stand with this center.

okr.objective: Explain quintessence as the Latin-derived distilled center named Mide.
key_results: State that the word moves from Latin for five to a distilled essence.
Place Mide as the center that is everywhere and nowhere, a turn point of the world.
Note Mide as one of five Irish provinces tied to no place before the medieval era.
Connect the center to Uisneach and Tara.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
